what_its_for: Permethrin is used to treat scabies (tiny mites that burrow into your skin and cause intense itching) and head lice (small insects that live in your hair and scalp). It works by paralyzing and killing the bugs and their eggs.
how_to_take: FOR SCABIES CREAM (5%): Wash your entire body with soap and water, then dry completely. Apply the cream from your neck down to the soles of your feet, including under your nails and in all skin folds. Leave it on for 8 to 14 hours (usually overnight), then wash it off completely in the shower. FOR HEAD LICE RINSE (1%): Wash your hair with regular shampoo (do NOT use a conditioner), then towel dry. Apply the rinse to your scalp and hair, leave it on for 10 minutes, then rinse thoroughly with water. Use the nit comb provided to remove lice and eggs from your hair.
dosing: SCABIES: One full-body application is usually enough. A second treatment may be needed 7 to 14 days later if live mites are still found. HEAD LICE: Apply once, then repeat after 7 to 10 days if live lice are still seen. For children, always follow the instructions on the package or as directed by your doctor or pharmacist.
missed_dose: Permethrin is usually used as a one-time or two-time treatment, not on a daily schedule. If you forgot to apply it on the day planned, apply it as soon as you remember. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed application. If you are unsure, ask your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, open flames, and direct sunlight. Keep the cap tightly closed and out of reach of children. Do not freeze. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not get permethrin in your eyes, nose, or mouth. If it gets in your eyes, rinse them thoroughly with water right away. Do not swallow it. Avoid using it on broken, cut, or irritated skin unless told to do so by your doctor. Do not use extra amounts or apply it more often than directed, as this will not work better and may cause more side effects. While being treated for head lice, avoid close head-to-head contact with others until treatment is complete. Wash all clothing, bedding, towels, and stuffed animals in hot water and dry on high heat to prevent re-infection.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get medical help right away if you experience: severe skin redness, rash, burning, or swelling after applying permethrin; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; your symptoms are not improving after completing treatment; you have a skin infection (signs include warmth, oozing, or crusting). Also call your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or if you need to treat an infant or young child, as special guidance is needed.
when_it_works: Itching from scabies may actually get WORSE for the first 1 to 2 weeks after treatment as your skin heals — this does NOT mean the treatment failed. Itching and irritation from scabies can take 2 to 4 weeks to fully go away. For head lice, dead lice may be visible within a few hours of treatment. You may still see empty egg shells (nits) in the hair after treatment — use a nit comb to remove them. Contact your doctor if you still see live moving lice or mites after completing both recommended treatments.
special_populations: CHILDREN: Permethrin 1% rinse can be used in children 2 months of age and older for head lice. The 5% cream for scabies may be used in infants as young as 2 months, but always follow your doctor's guidance. For infants, the cream may also need to be applied to the scalp, hairline, temples, and forehead. PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING: Permethrin is considered low-risk during pregnancy, but always talk to your doctor before using it. If breastfeeding, avoid applying the cream to the chest area and wash it off before nursing. ELDERLY: Elderly patients can generally use permethrin safely, but may have more sensitive skin. Use as directed and report any skin reactions to your doctor. PEOPLE WITH ALLERGIES: Do not use permethrin if you are allergic to chrysanthemums, ragweed, or other plants in the daisy family, as you may also be allergic to permethrin.
